title: Bessent PANICS as US Bonds Wipe Out Investors - Japan Just Lit a BIGGER Fuse
speaker: Sean Foo

macro_themes.view: 10y at 5.27%, a 19-year high; one of the worst bond bear markets in history with no guarantee yields stop rising, as Q4 issuance (~$630B) and war spending pile on.
Market prices ~99.7% odds of another hike by April; Bessent wants inflation to run hot and accepts a weaker dollar.
Coordinated US-Japan yen intervention and faster BOJ hikes could trigger a disorderly carry-trade unwind and broader US asset dump.
Canada pivoting trade to China/EU amid tariffs; dollar dominance could fade faster than expected.

calls.reason: War deficits, heavy Q4 issuance, Fed hikes and foreign selling (Japan) keep pushing yields higher.
calls.quote: There's simply no guarantee that yields will not go even higher.

calls.reason: Investor confidence shattered; structural inflation; possible Japanese selling of Treasuries.
calls.quote: US bonds have officially entered one of the worst bare markets in the entire history.

calls.reason: Dollar already fallen; Bessent accepts weaker dollar; coordinated yen intervention and trade diversion erode dollar demand.
calls.quote: The dollar's dominance could start fading faster than anyone really expects.

notes: Solo commentary (no guest). Yen strengthening expected via intervention but no instrument quoted, so not recorded. Date from listing; mentions oil fell ~$5 'yesterday'.
